title: Ophamin: a falsifiability-first experimentation framework with signed, cross-language-verifiable empirical proof records
description: Ophamin is a Python framework that turns experiments into signed empirical proof records. Every measurement is bound to its pre-registered falsifiable claim, to a byte-equal data corpus, to a versioned substrate-under-test, and to a tamper-evident HMAC-SHA256 signature; the verdict (VALIDATED / REFUTED / INCONCLUSIVE) is computed mechanically from the claim's threshold rather than chosen by the experimenter. The signed-record wire format is normatively specified in SCHEMAS.md (rules R1–R11) and verified byte-for-byte by read + write ports in Rust (crates/ophamin-proof) and JavaScript / TypeScript (packages/ophamin-proof-js); the round-trip is symmetric. Five interop layers wrap the same shared implementations: cross-language wire-format, an MCP server for agent-callable access, an HTTP REST API for service-style consumers, a CloudEvents 1.0 wrapper for event-stream interop, and OpenTelemetry instrumentation for production observability. The measurement-machinery tier includes seven cross-framework validation scenarios (Bayesian PyMC↔NumPyro, Wilson CI, Spearman, Pearson three-way, Welch's t-test three-way, one-way ANOVA three-way, Mann-Whitney U) — each a signed VALIDATED proof at floating-point agreement levels of ≤ 7×10⁻¹⁴.
